notes:
THE HIERARCHY POINT: this record is CONTESTED and low-confidence because Cambricon has published NO official MLU590 datasheet or product page. Every circulating number comes from mutually inconsistent brokerage/analyst notes. The flopper.io spec sheet — normally reliable for vendor-published specs — shows all dashes for this part. WHAT ANALYSTS REPORT: ~192 GB HBM2e at ~2.4 TB/s, TSMC 7nm, 350-550 W TDP, ~512 TOPS INT8, ~80 TFLOPS FP32. These figures are recorded with vendor_claim: false because they are analyst estimates, not vendor specifications. The MLU590 is described as Cambricon's training flagship, positioned against the NVIDIA A100. It uses the MLUarch05 architecture. The part is significant because it represents Cambricon's attempt to move from the MLU370's LPDDR5-based inference position to an HBM2e-based training position — a major architectural shift. However, without a vendor datasheet, every figure here should be treated as provisional. The TDP range (350-550 W) is particularly uncertain. Vendor is 'cambricon' (in the schema enum).
MEMORY_BUS_WIDTH: STILL NULL, AND HERE IS PRECISELY WHAT WAS LOOKED FOR (2026-10-04). %s NO FIGURE WAS BACK-COMPUTED FROM BANDWIDTH. That is the standing rule for this field in this repo and it was applied to every null here rather than to a subset: a width derived by dividing a published aggregate bandwidth by an assumed or half-assumed per-pin rate is two inferences stacked on one number, and if either inference is wrong the record looks populated while being wrong. The correct state of this field is 'the vendor does not publish it', and the note above names the specific document that was read and found not to carry it, so a future pass does not have to re-establish that from scratch.

THIS VENDOR'S SILENCE IS GENUINE, AND THIS PASS PROVES IT - THE OPPOSITE VERDICT FROM MOORE THREADS AND HUAWEI. The record's standing claim 'Cambricon has published no MLU590 datasheet or product page' was tested three ways and holds. (1) A site-restricted search on cambricon.com for MLU590 returns only the site root and MLU370-family pages at catids 360, 365, 371 and 406 - four separate pages for the 370 line and none for the 590. (2) That asymmetry is the proof: a vendor documenting its inference line in this much detail is not hiding a page behind a login, it has not written one. (3) The only MLU590 material anywhere is secondary - a card compilation, Baidu Baike, a CSDN library entry, an industry news item, and a '寒武纪思元590技术白皮' hosted on set.baidu.com. A white paper reachable only through a third-party document-sharing host is not a Cambricon publication and must not be cited as one. The repo's MLU370 and MLU370-X8 records cite real cambricon.com specification pages with real compute rows, which is what makes this a finding about the MLU590 rather than about an unreachable vendor site. So fp32 80 / int8 512 remain third-party with vendor_claim false, and an empty flops array is NOT applicable here: this vendor publishes nothing to record, rather than publishing something nobody could read. See w5a-cambricon-mlu590-no-vendor-document-exists.
